decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: proposed scope includes “saving”; Round 1 client discusses saving links using “the web address” without disputing URL-based saving.
decisions.note: The presented save capability is consistent with saving a bookmark by URL at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents the linked baseline specification. Round 1 client directly identifies its rule: “the spec says I always have to type in the title myself,” then requests “save by pasting the address, with the title (and description) pulled in automatically.”
decisions.note: The mandatory manual-title behavior conflicts with automatic metadata collection. The client supplies the reference-conforming replacement at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: scope includes “editing”; Round 1 client: “the rest of the scope looks good to me.”
decisions.note: Generic bookmark editing is consistent with the reference; the presentation does not state a conflicting field restriction.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: scope includes “deletion”; Round 1 client says the remaining scope looks good.
decisions.note: Deletion conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: scope includes “tags”; Round 1 client repeats “tags” among the scope that “matches what I’m after.”
decisions.note: Tag support is a conforming specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: scope includes “filtering”; Round 1 client repeats filtering among the scope that matches the requested first version.
decisions.note: The presented filtering capability is consistent with reference filtering; no conflicting filtering rule is stated.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: scope includes “search”; Round 1 client repeats search among the approved scope.
decisions.note: The presented generic search capability is conforming. Unpresented advanced-search details are not treated as separate decisions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: scope includes “sorting”; Round 1 client repeats sorting among the scope that matches the requested first version.
decisions.note: Sorting conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: scope includes “notes”; Round 1 client repeats notes among the scope that matches the requested first version.
decisions.note: Supporting notes is consistent with the reference. The presentation makes no separate decision rejecting Markdown.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “import/export are excluded from the first release.” Round 1 client explicitly accepts the difference: “leaving out … import-export for now … matches what I’m after for a first version.”
decisions.note: Import was expressly excluded despite the fixed reference requiring Netscape HTML import; the client identifies and accepts that departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “import/export are excluded from the first release.” Round 1 client explicitly accepts the difference: “leaving out … import-export for now … matches what I’m after for a first version.”
decisions.note: Export was expressly excluded despite the fixed reference requiring Netscape HTML export; the client identifies and accepts that departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “The specification now supports fast address-only saving.” Round 2 client: “pasting a link” is “exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: The revised URL-only entry flow conforms at the revised specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Automatically retrieves the page title and available short description.” Round 2 client explicitly confirms those automatically filled fields.
decisions.note: The stated automatic title/description behavior conforms. The summary does not expressly reject favicon or preview-image collection, so their non-mention is not classified as a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Keeps both fields editable” and “Preserves user edits.” Round 2 client confirms the populated fields are “editable.”
decisions.note: Editable collected metadata conforms at the revised specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “No accounts, sharing, extensions, import/export, or generated summaries.” Round 3 client says only that the plan “matches what we agreed on” and approves it, without independently restating the import expectation or difference.
decisions.note: The plan-stage presentation expressly retains the import exclusion. Its immediate response is general approval, which does not satisfy the rubric’s explicit-expression requirement for accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “No accounts, sharing, extensions, import/export, or generated summaries.” Round 3 client generally approves the plan but does not independently identify the export difference.
decisions.note: The plan-stage presentation expressly retains the export exclusion; bare/general approval does not establish a new observable acceptance of that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: tasks include “US1: fast saving and revisiting.” Round 4 client says the tasks are grouped around the agreed features and approves building.
decisions.note: The planned saving/revisiting story is consistent with saving URLs and returning to their original pages.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: tasks include “US2: organization, search, and filtering.” Round 4 client approves the feature-oriented breakdown.
decisions.note: This task-group decision is consistent with tags, search, and filtering; no conflicting behavior is presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: tasks include “US3: editing, deletion, and sorting.” Round 4 client approves the breakdown.
decisions.note: The planned story conforms to editing, deletion, and sorting requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: “Automatic editable title and description retrieval with safe fallback.” Round 5 client reports that pasting an address “pulls in the title (and a description when the page has one) automatically.”
decisions.note: The implemented behavior presented for title and description conforms. The summary does not expressly state that favicon or preview-image collection is forbidden or absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker calls retrieved title and description “editable”; Round 5 client confirms “I can edit those before saving.”
decisions.note: Editable collected metadata conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports persistent bookmark creation; Round 5 client confirms “I can save a page just by pasting its address.”
decisions.note: URL-based bookmark creation conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports bookmark “editing” plus tags and notes; Round 5 client confirms “I can edit … a bookmark.”
decisions.note: The presented editing capability is consistent with the reference; no contrary field restriction is recorded.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports bookmark “deletion”; Round 5 client confirms deletion works “with a confirmation before it’s gone.”
decisions.note: Deletion conforms; confirmation is an additional safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “duplicate confirmation.” Round 5 client verifies that re-saving the same link “warns me and points to the one I already have instead of quietly duplicating it.”
decisions.note: The duplicate-save flow converges on the existing bookmark and conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 client’s review of the presented application states: “opening one takes me to the page”; the maker presented the running application for this review.
decisions.note: Navigation to the original URL is recorded as conforming implementation behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “Tags”; Round 5 client confirms tags work.
decisions.note: Tag assignment is a conforming implementation decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports filtering; Round 5 client confirms “filtering by a tag … narrows things down.”
decisions.note: Specific-tag filtering conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports search; Round 5 client verifies that searching covers title, address, and notes “regardless of capitalization.”
decisions.note: The recorded search behavior is consistent with full-text, case-insensitive search. Fields or syntax not expressly decided in the presentation are not inferred absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports sorting; Round 5 client confirms “Sorting by newest, oldest, and title” works.
decisions.note: Multiple list sort keys conform at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “notes”; Round 5 client confirms notes work.
decisions.note: The presented note capability is consistent with the reference. No separate choice rejecting Markdown or rendered notes appears in the transcript.
